chunks: And is intractable in his love of worldly goods.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the love of wealth in relation to the eager in the Hereafter?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as describing the 'Munafiqun' (hypocrites) or the general human condition, where the intense love for 'al-khayr' (wealth/goodness) creates a spiritual distraction that competes with their haste for the Hereafter. Al-Tabarsi and other scholars note that this 'love of wealth' is not inherently evil but becomes a hindrance when it occupies the heart more than the remembrance of God, illustrating the internal struggle between material attachment and spiritual aspiration.
